description.value: A treed campground on Emory Creek's gold-rush-era townsite, 18 km north of Hope via Highway 1, with paved internal roads and easy access; the adjacent CP Rail mainline brings frequent train noise day and night.

address.value: 28625 Trans-Canada Hwy, Hope, BC V0X 1L3, Canada

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Emory Creek is an active BC Parks campground 18 km north of Hope on Hwy #1 with paved roads and flush outhouses, cooperatively managed with a community partner. OSM tags provide capacity (35 sites), fee status, no internet access, and phone. The website explicitly mentions cycling (bicycles must keep to roadways) and states e-bikes are not allowed on trails but permitted on park roads. A 'Reservation policies' section with a link to 'Frontcountry camping' indicates reservations are accepted. No amenities like showers, potable water, or food are mentioned on the fetched page.
concerns: OSM operator field says 'Yale First Nation' but website describes it as a BC Parks site cooperatively managed by a community partner — both may be accurate but the governance arrangement is ambiguous
No address available in OSM or on the website
Website notes this park is located next to the CPR mainline, which may mean train noise at night
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active provincial campground directly on Highway 1 near Hope, easily accessible by touring cyclists traveling through the Fraser Canyon. Facilities include flush outhouses and paved roads.

wow_evidence: gold-rush-era townsite, 18 km north of Hope via Highway 1
